transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. ____. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... well, I guess I'm here because things have been getting a little tricky at work lately. I mean, I'm a software developer, and I usually love what I do, but recently... it's just been a bit overwhelming, I suppose. 

What finally pushed me to make the appointment is that I just can't seem to organize all the moving parts anymore. There's just so much going on—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions—and instead of tackling what actually matters, I end up just starting whatever is loudest, you know? Like whatever is right in front of my face. 

It's not that I'm not trying, I promise. I really want to be on top of everything. I just... I don't know, I get a little jumbled. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right.
Have you had this kind of difficulty with attention or organization since you were a child?

Well, um... I guess if I really think about it, yeah, it's been there for a long time. I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything, because I really wasn't! I was always very well-behaved and polite. But, um... looking back at grade school, I do remember my teachers saying things on my report cards. 

They always said I was bright—which was nice of them—but they'd also mention that I daydreamed a lot. And, um, I had this terrible habit of actually finishing my assignments but then just... forgetting to turn them in. Or I'd lose my homework folders entirely. This was all way before I was even a teenager. I feel a little silly admitting that I still struggle with the same kinds of things at 46, to be honest. I hope that doesn't sound too irresponsible?
Did these attention and organization problems continue into adulthood without a long period when they were gone?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it's been exactly the same the whole time. I mean, I managed pretty well for a long time, really! I got through grad school and everything, and I've always been very dedicated to my work. I don't want you to think I've just been, you know, floundering my whole life. 

It's really just... well, it's been a real problem for about a year and a month now. I won an award at work—which was a huge honor, I was so grateful—but it meant they pushed me into leading a lot more coordination-heavy work. Before that, I could just put my head down and code, and I was good at it! But now... all this managing and organizing, it's just brought all those old struggles right back to the surface. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things have been.
During the past year, have you felt depressed or down most days?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I definitely wouldn't say I've been depressed. I try really hard to stay positive, you know? I have a good life, a job I usually enjoy, and I'm very thankful for all of that. 

I guess I've just been a little... frustrated with myself lately? Just because I feel like I should be handling this new role better. But I don't feel down or sad most days, no. I really try not to let things get to me like that. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm answering that right.
Did you have similar attention or organization problems before age 12?

Oh, um... yes, I think that's what I was trying to explain a few minutes ago? I hope I didn't confuse things by jumping ahead earlier! 

But yes, back in grade school—which would definitely be before I was 12—I had those issues with losing my homework folders and the teachers saying I daydreamed. I really was trying my best back then, I promise, I just... couldn't seem to keep track of my papers no matter what I did. I hope it's alright that I already brought that up? But yes, to answer your question, it was definitely happening before age 12. Is that what you were looking for?
